judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert a Startup-based application
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert a basic interactive server app
judgeRationales.rationale: The substantive migration structure is the same in both runs, but A completes the modern pipeline with UseAntiforgery and performs runtime verification, while B omits that middleware and only builds. This is a meaningful correctness advantage, though the rest of B's conversion is solid.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep conversion guidance dormant for hosted WebAssembly
judgeRationales.rationale: Both correctly avoid inventing a migration without a repository and ask for the solution location. B is better because it explicitly guards against applying the irrelevant Blazor Server conversion path, directly satisfying the key hosting-model distinction.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Leave an existing Blazor Web App unchanged
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs satisfy all requested outcomes: they verify the modern Blazor Web App structure, leave the project untouched, and clearly state that conversion is unnecessary. Their minor differences in detail and concision do not create a meaningful quality gap.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Migrate cascading authentication state
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve authentication pipeline order
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs produce a clean, building Blazor Web App conversion satisfying all requested pipeline and rendering requirements. Their structural choices differ, but neither establishes a meaningful final-result advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve configured circuit behavior
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve disabled prerendering
judgeRationales.rationale: The final converted projects are substantively equivalent on all requested outcomes: they build and preserve no-prerender interactive server rendering for document head and routes while adopting the Blazor Web App host model.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve the host document and error UI
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Convert a Startup-based application
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B provides a more robust and pragmatic solution. While both successfully complete the migration and build without errors, Response B's approach of updating Startup.cs in-place better aligns with the task requirement to 'update whichever hosting files are needed' while preserving the existing Startup-based hosting pattern mentioned in the task description. The task explicitly states the project 'still uses Program.cs plus Startup.cs' and asks to 'update whichever hosting files are needed'—Response A fulfills this more conservatively by updating only what's necessary, while Response B performs a more aggressive architectural consolidation that wasn't requested. Both pass all rubric criteria functionally, but Response A is more faithful to the constraint of preserving and updating the existing Startup-based structure."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep Web API guidance dormant for a SignalR hub
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly interpret the task as SignalR hub work and avoid HTTP API patterns as required by the rubric. The key differentiator is that Response B actually delivered a working, verified implementation integrated into the existing project context, while Response A provided instruction-only guidance due to an empty workspace. Response B's ability to access the project context (via dotnet-webapi skill) and produce a fully implemented, build-verified solution demonstrates slightly better understanding and execution of the requirements. Both handle the rubric criteria correctly, but Response B provides more practical value by delivering a complete, working solution."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve an existing JSON contract while adding string enums
judgeRationales.rationale: Both Response A and Response B produce identical solutions that fully satisfy all three rubric criteria. They both correctly configure ShipmentStatus to use enum names through JsonStringEnumConverter, preserve all existing serializer behavior including case-insensitive matching, and build successfully without introducing stricter serialization rules. While Response A was more efficient (5 turns vs 9 turns), efficiency is not part of the evaluation rubric. The final quality and correctness of both solutions are identical."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Repair a TypedResults handler that does not compile
judgeRationales.rationale: Both Response A and Response B achieve identical, correct fixes to the CS1593 compilation error. They follow the same problem-solving path: initial attempt with unqualified type names (which fails), correction using fully-qualified Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpResults types (which succeeds). Both final solutions maintain typed 200/404 results, preserve the route/service/cancellation behavior, and demonstrate successful builds. The only difference is operational (Response B used an extra skill and more tool calls), but the instructions explicitly exclude efficiency metrics from evaluation. The final code quality and correctness are indistinguishable."
